correctness.rationale: The positive exchangeable two-layer covariance splits into a scalar sector with variance theta(1-theta)/n and the standard sector H/[n(n-1)]. The resulting reproducing kernel has vanishing cross-rank constant part. Exact overlap probabilities yield R_1 and R_2, with the only potentially negative same-rank contribution from disjoint pair-pair comparisons. Direct differentiation proves R_1 strictly increasing, R_2 strictly decreasing, with unique meeting at theta=(n-1)/(n+1) and norm 3-4/n; n=3 is separately handled. Every row norm is attained by sign inputs. A complete exact-rational Gram-inversion verifier passes 46 parameter profiles and 1,061 individual row cases; symbolic derivatives and determinant identities are checked. Finite tests are auxiliary, while the proof treats all integers n>=3 and all 0<theta<1.

value.rationale: The first two nonempty ranks of the Boolean lattice form a natural finite sample geometry. Sharp bounded-input least-squares stability and positivity overshoot are meaningful analytical invariants; the theorem provides all-dimensional exact norms for every exchangeable mixture, identifies two distinct extremal row mechanisms and a unique minimax design, and links the sharp endpoint objective to but distinguishes it from known determinant-optimal designs. These are structural and optimization conclusions, not a reparameterized textbook projection identity or isolated small numeric improvement.
